correctness.rationale: I checked the coefficient by perturbing the periodic Floquet vector in the two eigenmodes of the unforced system, independently of the Riccati proof. A constant diagonal similarity symmetrizes the unforced off-diagonals to g=√(bc); its two eigenvalues differ by 2s, and the squared components of the principal unit vector are P=(1+r)/2 and L=(1−r)/2. In the orthonormal eigenbasis, the forced component along the other mode solves the periodic scalar equation with decay 2s and first-harmonic forcing of complex amplitude g(P exp(iφ)−L). The parallel first-order contribution to the quadratic average is the period mean of a derivative of a square, so it vanishes. Averaging the transverse response against the reverse coupling gives (g²/2) Re[(P−L exp(−iφ))(P exp(iφ)−L)/(2s+iω)], exactly the displayed Q. Analytic dependence of the monodromy and its simple positive leading eigenvalue holds in an amplitude neighborhood uniform on the compact phase circle; the half-period shift conjugates the monodromies for opposite amplitudes and removes odd terms. This gives the phase-uniform O(ε⁴). The first harmonic has nonzero cosine coefficient, ensuring a unique extremum of each kind for Q; its squared amplitude minus the squared offset is r²D, proving the two strict sign regions for r≠0 and the degenerate aligned case for r=0. In the aligned equal-rate case the matrices commute and average exactly; direct substitution also checks the frozen rational threshold witness. The optimizer and nondegenerate sign comparison are statements about the leading quadratic term, not a claim that the same phase exactly optimizes the full exponent at finite amplitude, nor a sign assertion at other zeros of Q. The supplied numerical checker is supplementary, not a proof.

value.rationale: A phase shift in a single periodic input can be removed by a time translation, but relative timing of two coupled inputs cannot. The calculation isolates the role of diagonal asymmetry in the relative-phase response, resolves the exactly commuting boundary, and provides a test case where equal means and equal forcing magnitudes do not determine the stability of a marginal two-state system. The value is the explicit perturbative classification of this idealized linear model, not a claim of operational, field, or finite-amplitude prediction.
